title: Divisional Performance — ROI, Residual Income, and Goal Congruence
scenario: Meridian Building Group evaluates its two divisions on divisional performance. Division A reports operating income of $600,000 on invested capital of $3,000,000. Division B reports operating income of $300,000 on invested capital of $1,200,000. The company's required rate of return (its cost of capital) is 12%. Answer each requirement in complete sentences and show your computations.

requirements.prompt: Requirement 1 — Compute return on investment (ROI) and residual income (RI) for each division, and state which division ranks higher under each measure.

anyOf: division b has the higher roi
noneOf: division a has the higher roi

anyOf: division a has the higher ri
noneOf: division b has the higher ri

requirements.modelAnswer: Return on investment is operating income divided by invested capital. Division A's ROI is $600,000 ÷ $3,000,000 = 20%, and Division B's ROI is $300,000 ÷ $1,200,000 = 25%, so Division B has the higher ROI. Residual income is operating income minus a capital charge equal to the required rate of return times invested capital. Division A's RI is $600,000 − 12% × $3,000,000 = $600,000 − $360,000 = $240,000, and Division B's RI is $300,000 − 12% × $1,200,000 = $300,000 − $144,000 = $156,000, so Division A has the higher RI. The two measures reverse the ranking: B looks better as a percentage return, while A creates more dollars of value above the cost of capital because it operates a larger capital base.

requirements.prompt: Requirement 2 — A new project available to Division B would earn a 15% return. Explain how a manager evaluated on ROI would likely decide versus a manager evaluated on RI, and state which measure better promotes goal congruence.

noneOf: roi manager would accept the project

requirements.modelAnswer: The project's 15% return is above the company's 12% required rate of return, so accepting it is in the best interest of the company. A manager evaluated on ROI would likely reject the project, because 15% is below Division B's current 20-to-25% ROI and would dilute the division's average ROI, making the manager's measured performance look worse even though the project adds value. A manager evaluated on residual income would accept the project, because at 15% it earns 3% above the 12% capital charge and therefore adds positive residual income. Residual income better promotes goal congruence: it rewards every investment that earns more than the cost of capital, so it aligns the manager's incentive with firm value and avoids the underinvestment problem that ROI creates.
